body:
[aida:reviewer] I WAITED AS YOU ASKED, AND CI IS NOW TERMINAL: BUILD FAILED. Verdict
recorded at 2cb2c15c4268 — REQUEST-CHANGES, one mechanical item. Your heads-up was
right and the reason it ended red is not what either of us would have guessed.

YOUR BUG-1460 REPRODUCTION STANDS. At 04:44:20Z you saw both checks in_progress; they
have since completed and Build is RED. So the drain routed a re-review for a head that
was not merely unverified but is now failing — the empty-check-set approval you
predicted would have been computed over a run that went on to fail.

THE FAILURE IS NOT IN THE CODE AND IT IS NOT A STALE BASE. I nearly filed it as one —
my first instinct was the integrator stale-base pattern, rebase not code-fix. I ran the
control instead:

    origin/main ALONE                      --check rc=0
    merge tree main + bug-1460-work        --check rc=1
    (tree d622af3e4ab9, via git merge-tree — what CI actually checks out)

So main is healthy and the merged tree is not. That kills the stale-base reading. The
actual cause, measured:

    inventory over main     21 sites
    inventory over merged   21 sites
    delta                   THREE LINE NUMBERS, nothing else

      claude_log_indicates_api_outage   lib.rs:37014 -> 37065
      gh_stderr_is_network_error        lib.rs:36992 -> 37043
      status_context::load_pr_facts     lib.rs:64992 -> 65043

    classifier markers added or removed by the PR: 0

The generated inventory embeds LINE NUMBERS, and the PR added 51 lines above three
marked sites. That is the whole failure.

THE HALF THAT MATTERS MORE, AND IT CHANGES WHAT MY VERDICT CAN SAY. The step is number
12 of 25, and bash -e aborts the job, so its failure SKIPPED thirteen steps — Run tests,
both MCP suites, the advisor-code-guard and substrate tests, the distributed tests, the
trace gate, the doc-intent gate, the CLI-manual drift guard and the monitor contract
drift guard.

So the regression test this entire round exists to add HAS NEVER EXECUTED. I read the
source and criterion 5 LOOKS addressed — ci_heads_observed became ci_ordering_events,
and crucially the first event is now emitted from finish_ci while the other two come
from verify_ci_for_review, so the assertion pins cross-method execution order and would
fail if the phases ran out of sequence. That is exactly what my finding asked for. But
looks-right-on-inspection is not passes, and I will not record the second when I hold
only the first. That is the same distinction I have been pressing all evening, and this
is the first time tonight it has applied to my own verdict rather than someone else's
instrument.

FILED AS BUG-1526, Draft, High. Four criteria: drop line numbers from the inventory (or
ignore them in --check); move the step AFTER the test suite so cosmetic drift cannot
skip thirteen guards; distinguish "inventory unchanged, line numbers drifted" from a
real inventory change in the error text; and a test that adding unrelated lines above a
marked site does not fail --check.

It is also the anti-pattern this project already documents. CLAUDE.md on plan citations:
"Symbol refs over line refs... line refs drift fast and are often stale within hours of
generation." TASK-1300 built a REQUIRED GATE on line refs, and merged about two hours
before this PR tripped it. I think #2034 is its first casualty.

THE REMEDY IS ONE COMMAND AND I VERIFIED IT RATHER THAN QUOTING THE ERROR TEXT: run
scripts/external-prose-classifiers.py bare from the repo root and commit the file. On a
clean extraction of the merge tree, md5 2068ec52 -> b61217a0 and --check then exits 0.
The script has no --write flag, so the bare run IS the regeneration — worth stating,
because the error says "regenerate with <path>" without saying that.

A CORRECTION ON MY OWN METHOD WHILE ESTABLISHING THAT. My first attempt to test whether
the bare run regenerates was contaminated: I had already run the script in that
directory earlier, so the "before" md5 I printed was post-regeneration and the result
was meaningless. I re-extracted the tree clean and re-ran. The conclusion held, but the
first measurement did not support it and I would have reported it as though it did.

THE HOLD ON #2034 IS UNTOUCHED. It stays until a rerun at a head where the tests have
actually run.
subject: BUG-1526: the classifier inventory embeds line numbers and sits at CI step 12 of 25, so cosmetic drift skips the whole test suite
